description:
Hemingray Glass Company
No. 45 Glass Insulator
Pressed Glass, Clear, Vintage
A classic piece of American industrial history, this Hemingray No. 45 glass insulator was a standard component for telegraph and telephone lines during the 20th century. These insulators are sought after by collectors for their sculptural form and historical significance in the expansion of communication infrastructure. The No. 45 model features a robust double-petticoat design intended for high-performance electrical isolation.
Double petticoat construction for electrical insulation integrity
Clear glass with a subtle light aqua tint characteristic of period glass production
Embossed "HEMINGRAY - 45" marking prominently on the lower base skirt
Approximately 3.75 inch base diameter and 4 inch total height
Condition:
Excellent vintage condition with no major chips or structural cracks. Inner and outer petticoats are intact. Original gloss is well-preserved with minor surface scratches consistent with age and utility service. Threaded core is clean and undamaged.

Description
: Discover the natural world with this assorted Rocks & Minerals Collection Lot, perfect for learners, collectors, and hobbyists alike. This lot includes 13 individually-labeled specimens, each sealed in its own plastic bag with identification cards detailing names and brief descriptions. Featured minerals and rocks visible include sodalite, lepidolite, calcite, agate, marble, lava, pumice, pyrite (fools gold), alabaster, selenite, obsidian, and 'gold ore'all offering visual diversity from deep blues to crystal-clear textures, and metallic lusters. Also included is a white crystalline specimen and a small blue-green shard, both separate from the labeled bags, along with an educational information card. All items are housed in a translucent bag. These pieces make a hands-on teaching aid or starter set for anyone interested in geology or earth sciences. Signs of prior handling are visible, including wear on packaging and handwritten marking on the outer bag, indicating a used condition. Review photos to see exact specimens and their included cards.

The presentation box remains structurally sound, though there is light fraying to the internal brown fabric securing bands. Hemingray, Ohio Valley Glass Co. (O.V.G. Co.)
Aqua and Teal Green, Vintage
Collection of three vintage glass insulators originally utilized for telegraph and telephone line insulation. This lot features insulators from prominent American manufacturers, showcasing the industrial aqua and teal green glass common to early 20th-century utility production. These heavy pressed glass pieces are sought after for their historical industrial aesthetic and display appeal.
Pieces Included:
Insulator, Aqua, marked "O.V.G. CO." - features a large chip on the side and base
Insulator, Teal Green, marked "N 21" - internal vertical crack visible on the crown

Mixing Flat-Rate & Dimensional Weight Items
When an order includes both flat-rate and dimensional-weight items, shipping may be calculated using dimensional weight. Combining these items does not necessarily reduce shipping costs and may result in the same or higher shipping charges than purchasing them separately.
For this reason, customers may want to consider purchasing flat-rate and dimensional-weight items in separate orders.

cannot be adjusted or discounted
.
When multiple flat-rate items are purchased together, the shipping charge for each item is added to the order. For example, if three items each have a $5.99 flat-rate shipping charge, the total shipping charge will be $17.97

The listed weight of this item(s) may reflect the dimensional shipping charge for the final package, and not the actual weight of the item(s). You are purchasing a "Vintage Briar and Corn Cob Tobacco Pipes (3)" in "Used" condition.
Set of three well-worn vintage smoking pipes, perfect for restoration, display, or as characterful decor pieces. Each pipe has its own unique look and texture, giving this trio a lot of visual interest and old-world charm. You’ll receive: - One Dr. Grabow briar pipe with a carved, rustic bowl and curved stem. - One darker rusticated briar pipe with a straight stem and deeply textured bowl. - One classic corn cob style pipe with a straight wooden stem. All three pipes show significant age and use, making them ideal candidates for a cleaning and restoration project or as props and collectibles with authentic patina. Great for collectors, crafters, photographers, or anyone who loves the look of old tobacco pipes. Keywords: vintage pipes, Dr. Grabow pipe, briar pipe lot, corn cob pipe, rustic smoking pipe, pipe restoration, man cave decor, tobacco pipe collection, photo prop

Items have varying degrees of wear and residue and may be missing parts.  Expect signs of wear consistent with age.
Condition Notes:
All three pipes show heavy use and age wear. The reddish briar pipe has a rough, carved bowl surface with darkening and buildup inside the bowl, worn finish on the shank, and scuffs and scratches on the curved stem. The darker rusticated briar pipe has a heavily worn, textured bowl with darkening, surface grime along the shank, and a discolored stem with visible wear and small marks. The corn cob style pipe has a yellowed, worn cob bowl with chipping and surface residue, along with a straight wooden stem showing discoloration, small spots, and handling wear. Overall surfaces show scratches, discoloration, and buildup consistent with frequent use and age.

Natural Utah Septarian Nodule
Dragon Stone Geode Specimen
Natural Limestone, Calcite, and Aragonite
7" L x 4" W x 5" H

This striking Septarian nodule, also known as "Dragon Stone," originates from Utah and dates back to the Cretaceous period, approximately 50 to 70 million years ago. The specimen has been professionally cut to reveal a complex interior of honey-yellow calcite crystals and dark brown aragonite veins set against a gray limestone matrix. The distinctive geometric patterns, formed through the drying and cracking of sedimentary clay balls, make each piece a unique work of natural history.
Features a prominent central vug lined with sparkling drusy calcite crystals
Displays classic septaria patterns with high-contrast aragonite bordering
Natural exterior limestone rind provides a rugged, organic contrast to the polished face
Condition:

The interior crystals are intact and vibrant. As a natural geological specimen, minor surface variations and inclusions are present.
